## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode #13855: TUI Home and End navigation in session prompts — restore cursor jump-to-start/end (SMALL priority, verify Alexi)

- **What**: Kilocode CLI's TUI session prompt input now correctly handles Home and End keys for cursor navigation (jump to start/end of line). Previously these keys were unmapped or captured by a parent container, so pressing Home/End did nothing. Fix restores standard readline-style navigation expected by CLI users. Likely involves explicit keypress handlers in the TUI input component or upgrading/patching `ink-text-input` to respect Home/End keypresses.
- **Why**: Home/End are standard readline navigation shortcuts (`^A` / `^E` equivalents). Breaking them frustrates users editing long prompts. Kilocode saw enough user reports to prioritize a fix.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13855 (fix(tui): restore Home and End navigation in session prompts)
- **Category**: command (TUI input navigation)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, ~1-2h. Alexi uses Ink v6.8.0 + `ink-text-input v6.0.0` (src/cli/tui/ confirmed). Verify that Home/End work in Alexi's prompt input (test in `ax chat` or `ax agent` interactive mode). If broken, check ink-text-input version compatibility or add explicit keypress handlers following Kilocode's fix pattern (likely in src/cli/tui/components/ or src/cli/interactive.ts).

#### 2. Aider #5173 + model settings commits: ANTHROPIC_MODELS expansion + Claude 4 temperature deprecation (SMALL priority, model catalog update)

- **What**: Aider expanded its `ANTHROPIC_MODELS` list (used by `sanity_check_models` to map bare Claude model names to `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) to include recent Claude models that were missing: `claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219`, `claude-opus-4-1` / `claude-opus-4-1-20250805`, `claude-opus-4-5` / `claude-opus-4-5-20251101`, `claude-opus-4-6-20260205` (dated), `claude-opus-4-7-20260416` (dated). Also added cross-provider settings for Claude Opus 4.7 (Bedrock/Vertex/OpenRouter variants) and deprecated `temperature` parameter for Claude 4 models (now disabled via explicit check). The list was stale — it had Claude 2, 3.x, 3-5-*, sonnet/opus-4 base names, but was missing these dated variants and the 3.7 Sonnet release.
- **Why**: Model catalogs must stay current with provider releases or users cannot invoke new models by name. Aider's keymap provider lookup falls through when a model is not in `ANTHROPIC_MODELS`, causing silent failures or wrong-provider selection. Temperature deprecation matters because Claude 4 rejects the parameter (API error), so sending it breaks requests.
- **Source**: https://github.com/aider-ai/aider/pull/5173 (Expand ANTHROPIC_MODELS list with recent Claude model names), plus commits for GPT-5.5 model settings, Claude Opus 4.7 Bedrock/Vertex/OpenRouter, temperature disable for Claude 4
- **Category**: provider (model catalog)
- **Size**: SMALL priority, ~1-2h. Check Alexi's model catalog (src/providers/modelCatalog.ts) for these model IDs. If missing, add them with appropriate metadata (context window, cost, capabilities). Also verify that Alexi's SAP AI Core provider (src/providers/sapOrchestration.ts) does NOT send `temperature` to Claude 4 models (check formatModelRequest or similar). Cross-provider variants (Bedrock/Vertex/OpenRouter) are not immediately relevant (Alexi uses SAP AI Core), but the core Anthropic model IDs are.

#### 3. Kilocode #13541: VS Code PR review comments inline in diffs — show GitHub review comments in diff view (LOW priority, VS Code-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode VS Code extension now displays PR review comments inline in the diff view (likely the side-by-side or unified diff panel) so users can see reviewer feedback without switching to the GitHub web UI. Comments are fetched via `gh pr view --json comments,reviews` and rendered as decorations or hover tooltips at the relevant line numbers.
- **Why**: Addressing review feedback requires seeing both the code change and the comment. Forcing users to toggle between VS Code and GitHub web breaks flow. Inline comments close the gap.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13541 (feat(vscode): show PR review comments inline in diffs)
- **Category**: command (VS Code UI)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no VS Code extension, no diff view UI, no PR review comment integration. This is desktop-IDE-specific. Not CLI-portable. (Alexi CLI equivalent is manual: `gh pr view --json comments | jq -r '.comments[] | "\(.path):\(.line) \(.body)"'`, which is the CLI-native pattern for reviewing comments.)

#### 4. Kilocode #13848: CLI shared agent board messages display fix — show shared board messages (LOW priority, board-specific)

- **What**: Kilocode CLI's agent board (shared message surface for multi-agent coordination) was not displaying messages correctly — likely a rendering bug where shared board posts were fetched but never rendered in the TUI. Fix ensures that `board` tool messages are displayed in the CLI agent view.
- **Why**: The board is a coordination surface for multi-agent workflows. If messages are not displayed, agents cannot see each other's state updates or handoff signals, breaking the orchestration.
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13848 (fix(cli): show shared agent board messages)
- **Category**: command (CLI TUI)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has a `board` tool (src/tool/tools/board.ts confirmed) but may not have the same TUI message-display bug. This is a Kilocode-specific rendering regression fix. Not immediately actionable unless Alexi users report similar board message visibility issues.

#### 5. Kilocode #13847 + #13794: VS Code subagent transcript performance + undo/redo containment (LOW priority, VS Code-specific)

- **What**: Two VS Code extension fixes: (1) #13847 improves subagent transcript rendering performance (likely virtualizing large message lists or debouncing updates to prevent UI lag when a subagent generates many messages rapidly), (2) #13794 keeps prompt undo/redo history inside the webview (prevents Ctrl+Z from undoing editor changes outside the agent prompt panel).
- **Why**: Subagent transcripts can grow large (100+ messages) during long autonomous runs, and re-rendering every message on each update causes lag. Undo/redo leaking outside the prompt panel is a UX bug (user expects Ctrl+Z to undo prompt text, not editor changes).
- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13847 (fix(vscode): improve subagent transcript performance), https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/13794 (fix(vscode): keep prompt undo and redo inside the webview)
- **Category**: command (VS Code UI performance + undo/redo isolation)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no VS Code extension, no webview-based subagent transcript rendering. These are desktop-IDE-specific performance/UX fixes. Not CLI-portable.

#### 6. Aider #5132: Bash tree-sitter tags for repomap support — enable function/variable extraction from Bash scripts (MODERATE priority, defer)

- **What**: Aider added tree-sitter tags for Bash (function definitions, variable assignments) to its repomap feature (codebase outline / symbol index used by the agent for context selection). Previously Bash scripts were indexed as flat text; now Aider can extract and display `function foo() { ... }` and `VAR=value` symbols in the repomap, improving agent context awareness for shell-heavy projects.
- **Why**: Repos with significant Bash scripting (build scripts, deployment automation) need function-level navigation. Without tree-sitter tags, the agent cannot see which functions exist or where they are defined, degrading context selection quality.
- **Source**: https://github.com/aider-ai/aider/pull/5132 (feat: add bash tree-sitter tags for repomap support)
- **Category**: tool (code indexing / repomap)
- **Size**: MODERATE priority, DEFER. Alexi has `definitions` tool (src/tool/tools/definitions.ts) but does not expose a repomap/symbol-index surface yet. Bash tree-sitter tags would be useful for repos with heavy shell scripting, but Alexi's current tooling (grep, codesearch, definitions) is enough for now. Keep on radar for future repomap/symbol-index work.

- **What**: OpenCode console now publishes an OAuth client metadata document (likely `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` or OIDC discovery endpoint) so OAuth clients can discover authorization/token endpoints programmatically instead of hardcoding them. Standard OAuth 2.0 / OIDC feature.
- **Why**: Hardcoded OAuth endpoints break when the console's domain or URL structure changes. Discovery documents make OAuth integration more robust.
- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/47737 (feat(console): publish oauth client metadata document)
- **Category**: config (OAuth discovery)
- **Size**: LOW priority, SKIP — Alexi has no OAuth console, no client authentication flow, no OIDC discovery. This is OpenCode-console-specific. Not CLI-portable.
